plain: To spread out into a wider variety

webster.text: To make different or various in form or qualities; to give variety to; to variegate; as, to diversify the colors of a robe; to diversify a landscape with mountains, plains, trees and lakes.

example.quote: To diversify and extend these improvements is the surest and safest method of indemnifying ourselves for any inconveniences which those or similar measures have a tendency to beget.
example.cite: Alexander Hamilton, Report on Manufactures (communicated to the House of Representatives, Dec. 5, 1791)
